polls.study: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel August 2026
polls.geographic_population: US adults aged 18 and older, not all worldwide YouTube users

content_types.scope: reported current affairs or independently attributed journalism
nonpartisan explanation of institutions, ballots and processes
substantive discussion of proposed or implemented public policy
explicit argument or ideological opinion by the publisher
satirical or comedic treatment of events
insufficient context or more than one distinct type

event_window_design.require_comparable: same topic/query, geography, language and API parameters; fixed observation capture schedule
warnings: Search results are relevance-filtered and incomplete; totalResults is an estimate, not an upload census.
regionCode restricts viewable videos and is not the residence of actual viewers or creator.
relevanceLanguage is a ranking preference, not verified audio or creator language.
Published-after/before is upload time, not when an audience watched content.
Use fixed pre/post periods and comparable sources; views accumulated since upload are age-confounded.
Changes in platform ranking, real-world events and competitor posts confound non-random historical contrasts.

google_trends.population: sampled Google Search interest for a chosen term/time/geography; not YouTube video discovery

constraints: Research content topics and visible public channel output, never individual viewers' political identity or susceptibility.
Descriptive surveys of aggregate party affiliation are not estimates of any individual channel audience.
Do not rank political groups or recommend demographic-targeted persuasion or political advertising tactics.
Pew source estimates are 2026 U.S. adult self-reports; yearly survey percentages are not global news viewers or video impressions.
Google Trends 0–100 index cannot be converted to absolute searches or to YouTube searches.
YouTube search.list is discovery metadata, not exhaustive platform uploads, audience size, unique viewers or causal impact.
Reuters's 48-market weekly YouTube news survey and Pew's U.S. adult regular news survey are different definitions and denominators, even where both show 34%; do not pool or rank political audiences.

reuters_video_news_survey.sample_frame: online news survey respondents in 48 selected markets; not a probability sample of the entire world
caveats: Reuters figures come from sampled online respondents across 48 markets, not a global platform person count.
Weekly 34% YouTube-for-news in cross-market Reuters reporting is not Pew's separately sampled 34% of U.S. adults reporting regular YouTube news use.
Regional news-video survey questions and exposure mechanisms are not a measurement of political commentary exclusively or verified public video views.
Intentional versus incidental responses are conditional on YouTube news consumers, not all adults or watchers of specific channels.
A newsroom clip, independent creator and commentary can overlap and cannot be apportioned from public aggregate figures to known total audiences.
Different Reuters report chapters reuse a common 2026 report family and do not constitute independent surveys.
No audience ideology, partisan identity, influence, voter behavior or advertising return of a channel was measured.
